title: Hosted backstop capacity negotiation and degradation controls
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: Design and implement a negotiated "backstop" interface and degradation control flow used when tenant-dedicated capacity is exhausted and requests are routed to hosted infrastructure. The goal is to provide predictable latency/cost behavior, maintain tenant isolation guarantees where required, and allow graceful quality degradation (variant downgrades) with transparent accounting. This ticket captures the protocol, implementation plan, SLO implications, telemetry requirements, and runbook for on-call handling.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy orchestration implements a capacity negotiation handshake (LeaseRequest / LeaseResponse) between dedicated pool and hosted backstop with 99th-percentile handshake latency <50ms within region

Three-stage degradation strategy implemented: (1) exact same model on hosted, (2) quantized/fast variant, (3) smaller model fallback. Each stage must have per-tenant opt-in/opt-out and cost estimation returned in response headers
Per-tenant safety throttle and emergency-stop flag that prevents spillover for regulated tenants (RBAC-guarded) is enforced in orchestrator
Telemetry emitted for every spillover decision: reason, capacity_token, latency_headroom, model_variant, cost_delta — visible in Console per-tenant dashboard
End-to-end tests that simulate dedicated exhaustion and validate correct variant selection, billing attribution, and rollback mechanisms are added to CI
tasks: Spec: finalize handshake protocol and message fields (Maya) — include lease_duration, estimated_cost, priority_score, latency_headroom
Orchestrator: implement LeaseRequest/LeaseResponse state machine and metrics (Evan)
Runtime: add variant tags and fast-quantized model routing paths (Runtime team)
Console: surface spillover events and per-tenant cost estimate in route trace (Console UX)
Billing: ensure hosted-backed requests are attributed to tenant and draft billing model for hybrid spillover
E2E: create failure-injection harness to simulate capacity exhaustion and latency spikes
Security/Compliance: review emergency-stop RBAC paths and audit logging
Docs: write dev guide and migration notes for Dedicated customers
decision_log: 2026-02-14: Rejected 'naive passthrough' approach where orchestrator simply forwards to hosted without negotiation — lacked tenant visibility and cost transparency
2026-02-18: Chosen approach: lease-based negotiation with short-lived tokens (default 30s) and conservative lease extension to avoid surprise amplification
2026-02-22: Degradation tiers agreed: same-architecture hosted variant > int8-quantized variant > distilled smaller model; no automatic semantic-altering rewrites as first step
2026-03-03: Opt-in enforcement model chosen for regulated tenants — default to block spillover unless tenant explicitly allows; enforcement at control-plane with audit trail
comments: Maya (2026-02-12): Initial draft of handshake proto posted in doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/routing/backstop-handshake-v1
Evan (2026-02-16): Impl note — we must ensure orchestration proxy can operate at line rate; will prototype in go with a memory-light state cache
Kunal (SRE, 2026-02-24): Suggest adding a circuit-breaker based on queued waiting time, not just instantaneous GPU utilization
Product (2026-03-01): PM requests per-tenant UI to allow customers to set preferred degradation order and hard-block list
Security (2026-03-05): Require HMAC-signed lease tokens and KMS-backed signing for hosted acceptance to prevent token forgery
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind 'hosted_backstop_v1' flag; 2) Canary with internal alpha tenants in us-west-2 (5% traffic) for 72h; 3) Expand to small set of non-regulated customers (20%) with metrics guardrails; 4) Full open rollout in region if error rate and cost drift within thresholds for 7 days
rollback_plan: Disable 'hosted_backstop_v1' flag to revert to legacy dedicated-first routing; kill any outstanding leases and surface a rollback incident; notify affected tenants via status page and provide follow-up remediation steps
